misconceptions.description: Running a bulk action like a mail merge or rename script on real files before testing on a small sample
misconceptions.trigger: learner runs a rename macro on the whole folder and corrupts 200 files at once
misconceptions.feedback: Test on a copy of two or three files first. Confirm the result, then run the automation on the full set.

misconceptions.description: Deleting rows after a spreadsheet filter without realizing hidden rows can be affected or that the filter is still active
misconceptions.trigger: learner filters to 'overdue', deletes, then finds the wrong rows gone when the filter clears
misconceptions.feedback: Before deleting filtered rows, copy the kept rows to a new sheet, or sort instead of filter, so you can see exactly what goes.

misconceptions.description: Writing an email auto-rule so broad it sweeps important messages into a folder you never check
misconceptions.trigger: a rule 'if contains class, move to Archive' also hides advisor and registrar mail
misconceptions.feedback: Make rules specific (match sender plus subject) and review the target folder, so a rule never silently buries something you need.

misconceptions.description: Triggering an automation that cannot be undone without first making a backup or confirming an undo path
misconceptions.trigger: learner empties trash or overwrites a synced file with no copy to recover
misconceptions.feedback: Before an irreversible automation, save a backup copy and confirm there is an undo or version history to fall back on.
